misconceptions.description: Treating instructional design as content formatting only
misconceptions.trigger: learner describes ID as slide creation or media production without analysis or evaluation
misconceptions.feedback: Instructional design is broader than content packaging. It includes diagnosing learner needs, defining objectives, designing assessments, and evaluating whether the intervention solved the performance gap.

misconceptions.description: Assuming one learning theory is universally correct
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims behaviorism, cognitivism, or constructivism should always be used in every context
misconceptions.feedback: Strong instructional design is pragmatic. Different theories support different goals: behaviorism for fluency and habits, cognitivism for processing and load management, constructivism for meaning-making and transfer.

misconceptions.description: Interpreting ADDIE as a rigid one-pass sequence in every modern context
misconceptions.trigger: learner says ADDIE cannot be iterative or adapted
misconceptions.feedback: ADDIE is often used today as a flexible systems framework rather than a rigid waterfall. Teams frequently iterate within and across phases.
